chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz from Ayub ibn Nuh, both together, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding the woman, when the news of her husband's death reaches her, he said: She observes the waiting period (Iddah) from the day the news reaches her, as if she is mourning for him.
ai.seo_question: When does a widow's waiting period begin if her husband dies while he was away?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the starting point of the Iddah for a widow whose husband died during his absence, establishing that the period commences upon the actual receipt of the news rather than the date of death. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for resolving disputes regarding the duration of waiting when the exact time of death is unknown, ensuring the widow's observance of mourning is tied to her awareness of the event.
